title: Re-roll 2: modern, product-grade, with personality
question: Steered toward designer-engineer portfolios. The roll assigned the annotated notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Annotated: an engineer's notebook
options.lineage: sidenote typography (Tufte) as practiced on the best designer-engineer sites
options.thesis: Plain facts in the main column, and the margin talks back: small live demos, asides in his own voice, the reasoning behind each piece of work.
options.viewport: Left main column: "Qwertic. AI engineer, full stack." and three plain sentences with Book a call. Right margin, aligned line by line: a live miniature of the human-review flow (a synthetic document, extracted fields, an approve step), labelled as a demo.
options.risk: Can read as a quiet blog if the margin demos are timid; the margin has to be the memorable part.

raised.raise: A fixed row of six plain facts up top (role, base, availability, current work, stack, contact) that the rest of the page cross-checks.
Main column and margin answer each other across the gutter, line for line, never floating loose.
One accent colour, used only for the thing currently live or moving.
No drop shadows: layers read by overlap and rules only.

options.label: Working interface: the site is a small product
options.lineage: product sites where the demo is the hero
options.thesis: Don't describe the AI work, run it: the homepage opens on a live synthetic version of the document to extraction to human review flow, with a ⌘K palette as navigation.
options.viewport: Headline left, and on the right a working mini-app: drop a sample CV, watch fields extract, approve or correct them. Book a call under the headline.
options.risk: This is where most designer-engineer sites land; it's familiar and effective, but less personal.

options.label: ASCII live render
options.thesis: A live scene drawn entirely in typed characters: a Q keycap turning, made of glyphs, above plain text.
options.viewport: A rotating keycap rendered in ASCII over half the screen, with QWERTIC, the role line and Book a call set in the same grid.
options.case: Fuses well on personality and engineer appeal (the keyboard is in the name). Loses narrowly on clarity for non-technical visitors.
options.risk: Dark mono reads as a hacker cliché unless the text around it is calm and plain.

options.label: Night-flight instruments
options.case: Loses on both counts: a metaphor that needs decoding.
options.kept: A fixed set of facts that cross-check each other.

options.label: Bazaar spread
options.thesis: Didot and photographs dancing across the gutter.
options.case: Loses on both counts: editorial luxury, not product-grade.
options.kept: Two columns answering each other across the gutter.

options.label: Japanese high-density web
options.case: Loses on both counts: too dense for a first visit.
options.kept: The courage to pack real detail at small sizes.

options.label: Paper automata
options.thesis: A crank turns and figures move.
options.case: Loses on both counts: whimsical, off-brief.
options.kept: One accent reserved for what's moving.

options.label: Łowicz papercut
options.case: Loses on both counts: folk craft, unrelated to the work.
options.kept: Depth by overlap, never by shading.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean designer-engineer portfolio, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one line, a short list of work and writing, contact.
canonCard.risk: Clean and familiar by design; the personality has to come from the details.
